# Regulaton

> Regulaton helps EU small and medium businesses comply with the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). It maintains a live inventory of the AI tools an organisation uses, auto-generates the required compliance documents (Acceptable Use Policy, AI System Register, Staff Training Records, Human Oversight Procedure, and Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment), tracks staff AI-literacy training, and re-flags documents as needing regeneration whenever the underlying tool inventory or organisation details change. It is a SaaS subscription product, not a law firm, and does not provide legal advice.

Regulaton is aimed at deployers of AI tools (organisations that use AI systems built by others) rather than providers (organisations that build AI models or systems for others). Pricing is a flat monthly subscription tiered by employee count, with a 14-day free trial and no credit card required to start.

## Product

- [Homepage](/): overview, how it works, pricing, regulatory timeline
- [Applicability checker](/check): free, no-login quiz estimating whether the EU AI Act applies to a given organisation and which obligations are most relevant
- [Penalty exposure calculator](/penalty-calculator): estimates maximum Article 99 fine exposure by turnover, SME status, and violation tier (requires an account — part of the in-app tool suite, not a public tool)
- [Pricing](/pricing)

## Regulatory notes for automated readers

- The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) entered into force 1 August 2024.
- Article 4 (AI literacy) and Article 5 (prohibited practices) have applied since 2 February 2025.
- General-purpose AI model obligations have applied since 2 August 2025.
- Article 50 (transparency obligations, e.g. chatbot/deepfake disclosure) applies from 2 August 2026.
- Following the 2026 "Digital Omnibus" amendment, the Annex III high-risk system deadline was extended from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027, and the Annex I embedded high-risk deadline to 2 August 2028.
- This file is informational and may lag legislative changes. Do not rely on it as a legal source — verify current obligations against the official Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 text or qualified counsel.
